title: Quick Trade Analytics Maturity Scan
description: 24 high-signal questions answerable by a customs director in 10 minutes

questions.questionText: Does your customs administration have a documented digital transformation strategy?

levelDescriptions.1: No digital transformation strategy exists. Operations are paper-based.
levelDescriptions.2: Informal modernization goals discussed but not documented.
levelDescriptions.3: Board-approved digital strategy aligned with WCO Framework of Standards.
levelDescriptions.4: Digital strategy drives budget allocation with measurable KPIs.
levelDescriptions.5: Continuously refined strategy using performance data and WCO benchmarks.

questions.questionText: Is your modernization aligned with WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) commitments?

levelDescriptions.1: No TFA alignment. Category C notifications pending.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic awareness of TFA obligations but limited implementation.
levelDescriptions.3: TFA Category A measures implemented. Category B timeline set.
levelDescriptions.4: Full TFA Category A+B compliance with capacity building for C.
levelDescriptions.5: All TFA measures implemented with continuous improvement monitoring.

questions.questionText: Does leadership actively champion data-driven customs modernization?

levelDescriptions.1: No executive sponsor for analytics or modernization.
levelDescriptions.2: IT department informally leads modernization efforts.
levelDescriptions.3: Dedicated DG-level sponsor with modernization mandate.
levelDescriptions.4: Cross-agency steering committee with ministerial support.
levelDescriptions.5: National trade facilitation committee with analytics-driven agenda.

questions.questionText: Is there a dedicated data analytics unit within customs?

levelDescriptions.1: No dedicated analytics roles. IT handles basic reporting.
levelDescriptions.2: A few analysts exist but without formal structure.
levelDescriptions.3: Dedicated analytics unit with defined roles and mandate.
levelDescriptions.4: Specialized teams (risk, revenue, trade facilitation) with analytics skills.
levelDescriptions.5: Analytics talent embedded across all customs operations with career paths.

questions.questionText: Do customs officers receive training in data analytics and modern tools?

levelDescriptions.1: No analytics training. Officers use only legacy systems.
levelDescriptions.2: Occasional workshops on basic Excel reporting.
levelDescriptions.3: Structured training program with BI tools and data literacy.
levelDescriptions.4: Advanced analytics training including statistics and ML concepts.
levelDescriptions.5: Continuous learning program with certifications and WCO academy courses.

questions.questionText: Is there collaboration between customs, border agencies, and trade stakeholders on data?

levelDescriptions.1: Siloed operations. No data sharing between agencies.
levelDescriptions.2: Ad-hoc data requests between agencies.
levelDescriptions.3: Formal data sharing agreements with key agencies.
levelDescriptions.4: Integrated data platform shared across border agencies.
levelDescriptions.5: Real-time coordinated border management with unified analytics.

questions.questionText: Has your country published a WCO Data Model My Information Package (MIP)?

levelDescriptions.1: No awareness of WCO DM MIP concept.
levelDescriptions.2: Awareness of WCO DM but no MIP development started.
levelDescriptions.3: MIP development in progress with partial WCO DM mapping.
levelDescriptions.4: Published MIP covering all customs procedures.
levelDescriptions.5: Comprehensive MIP with regular updates aligned to WCO DM releases.

questions.questionText: Are data quality standards defined for customs declarations and trade data?

levelDescriptions.1: No data quality standards. High error rates in declarations.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic validation rules in electronic filing system.
levelDescriptions.3: Documented data quality standards with periodic audits.
levelDescriptions.4: Automated data quality monitoring with rejection and correction flows.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-driven data quality with predictive error detection.

questions.questionText: Is there a master data management strategy for traders, tariffs, and commodities?

levelDescriptions.1: No master data management. Duplicate records are common.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic trader registration but no systematic MDM.
levelDescriptions.3: Master data governance for traders and tariff codes.
levelDescriptions.4: Enterprise MDM with golden records and automated matching.
levelDescriptions.5: Real-time MDM with AI-assisted entity resolution and enrichment.

questions.questionText: Is your customs system integrated with a National Single Window (PSW)?

levelDescriptions.1: No single window. Paper-based clearance with multiple agencies.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic electronic filing but separate systems per agency.
levelDescriptions.3: PSW operational with basic inter-agency data sharing.
levelDescriptions.4: Full PSW integration with automated cross-agency workflows.
levelDescriptions.5: Advanced PSW with real-time risk sharing and coordinated border management.

questions.questionText: Can you track a shipment end-to-end from origin to clearance?

levelDescriptions.1: No shipment tracking. Status only known at customs point.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic status tracking within customs system only.
levelDescriptions.3: Integration with shipping lines and freight forwarders for tracking.
levelDescriptions.4: End-to-end visibility with carrier, port, and customs data linked.
levelDescriptions.5: Predictive shipment analytics with estimated arrival and risk pre-screening.

questions.questionText: Does your data architecture conform to WCO Data Model standards?

levelDescriptions.1: Proprietary data formats with no WCO DM alignment.
levelDescriptions.2: Awareness of WCO DM but customs system uses legacy schema.
levelDescriptions.3: Partial WCO DM conformity for key data elements.
levelDescriptions.4: Full WCO DM conformity across all customs procedures.
levelDescriptions.5: WCO DM native architecture with automated conformity validation.

questions.questionText: Is risk-based selectivity for inspections driven by analytics?

levelDescriptions.1: Random or 100% inspection with no risk-based selectivity.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic rule-based selectivity (e.g., country of origin, HS code).
levelDescriptions.3: Statistical risk profiling with historical compliance data.
levelDescriptions.4: ML-based risk scoring with multiple data sources and real-time updates.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-driven predictive risk with network analysis and behavioral profiling.

questions.questionText: Are predictive models used for revenue forecasting or fraud detection?

levelDescriptions.1: No predictive models. Revenue estimates are manual.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic trend analysis using historical data.
levelDescriptions.3: Statistical models for revenue forecasting.
levelDescriptions.4: ML models for fraud detection and revenue optimization in production.
levelDescriptions.5: Ensemble models with real-time fraud alerts and automated interventions.

questions.questionText: Do you use analytics for customs valuation verification?

levelDescriptions.1: Manual valuation checks with no analytical support.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic price database for comparison only.
levelDescriptions.3: Transaction value database with statistical outlier detection.
levelDescriptions.4: ML-based valuation models with transfer pricing detection.
levelDescriptions.5: Real-time valuation intelligence with global price benchmarking.

questions.questionText: Is your customs IT infrastructure cloud-enabled or modernized?

levelDescriptions.1: Legacy mainframe or client-server systems only.
levelDescriptions.2: Some web-based applications but core systems are legacy.
levelDescriptions.3: Hybrid infrastructure with cloud for some workloads.
levelDescriptions.4: Cloud-first architecture with elastic scaling.
levelDescriptions.5: Multi-cloud platform with serverless processing and edge computing.

questions.questionText: Can your systems handle the current declaration volume with acceptable performance?

levelDescriptions.1: System slowdowns and outages during peak periods.
levelDescriptions.2: Adequate for current volume but no headroom for growth.
levelDescriptions.3: Scalable architecture handling 2-3x current volume.
levelDescriptions.4: Auto-scaling infrastructure with sub-second response times.
levelDescriptions.5: Globally distributed platform handling any volume with 99.99% uptime.

questions.questionText: Do you have a centralized data warehouse for trade analytics?

levelDescriptions.1: No data warehouse. Analytics done on operational databases.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic reporting database with periodic data extracts.
levelDescriptions.3: Enterprise data warehouse with scheduled ETL from customs systems.
levelDescriptions.4: Modern data platform with real-time ingestion and analytics.
levelDescriptions.5: Lakehouse architecture with streaming, ML, and unified governance.

questions.questionText: What percentage of customs declarations are filed electronically?

levelDescriptions.1: Less than 20% electronic. Most declarations are paper-based.
levelDescriptions.2: 20-50% electronic filing through WeBOC or equivalent.
levelDescriptions.3: 50-80% electronic filing with remaining paper for special cases.
levelDescriptions.4: 90%+ electronic filing with exception-only paper processing.
levelDescriptions.5: 100% electronic with automated processing and straight-through clearance.

questions.questionText: Is there an Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) program with data-driven benefits?

levelDescriptions.1: No AEO program or trusted trader concept.
levelDescriptions.2: AEO framework exists but limited implementation.
levelDescriptions.3: Operational AEO program with compliance-based benefits.
levelDescriptions.4: Data-driven AEO with continuous monitoring and dynamic benefits.
levelDescriptions.5: Mutual recognition with other countries and AI-based compliance scoring.

questions.questionText: Is post-clearance audit driven by analytics and risk assessment?

levelDescriptions.1: No systematic post-clearance audit program.
levelDescriptions.2: Random post-clearance audits with no analytics input.
levelDescriptions.3: Risk-based audit selection using historical compliance data.
levelDescriptions.4: Analytics-driven audit with predictive targeting and revenue recovery.
levelDescriptions.5: Continuous compliance monitoring with automated audit triggers.

questions.questionText: Can you measure the impact of trade facilitation measures on clearance times?

levelDescriptions.1: No measurement of clearance times or facilitation impact.
levelDescriptions.2: Manual Time Release Studies conducted occasionally.
levelDescriptions.3: Automated clearance time tracking with regular TRS reporting.
levelDescriptions.4: Real-time performance dashboards with trend analysis.
levelDescriptions.5: Predictive analytics for clearance time optimization with SLA management.

questions.questionText: Has analytics measurably increased customs revenue collection?

levelDescriptions.1: No evidence of analytics impact on revenue.
levelDescriptions.2: Some revenue recovery from ad-hoc investigations.
levelDescriptions.3: Documented revenue uplift of 3-5% from analytics-driven interventions.
levelDescriptions.4: Systematic revenue optimization achieving 5-15% improvement.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-driven revenue assurance with predictive leakage detection.

questions.questionText: Do you share trade intelligence with other government agencies and WCO?

levelDescriptions.1: No trade intelligence sharing beyond customs.
levelDescriptions.2: Ad-hoc information sharing on specific cases.
levelDescriptions.3: Formal intelligence sharing framework with key agencies.
levelDescriptions.4: Real-time intelligence sharing via Regional Intelligence Liaison Office.
levelDescriptions.5: Automated cross-border intelligence with WCO CEN and partner countries.
